topic: Planning Commission and History of Economic Planning
description: Economic planning in India was adopted to achieve rapid economic growth and socio-economic justice through the optimum utilization of national resources. The Planning Commission was established in 1950 as the premier institution to formulate and implement the iconic Five-Year Plans.

sections.title: Pre-Independence Efforts for Economic Planning
sections.description: Before India gained independence, various scholars, industrialists, and political leaders proposed foundational blueprints for the economic development of the country.

historical_events.significance: A seminal book written by Sir M. Visvesvaraya, which proposed a 10-year plan for India, marking the first academic attempt at economic planning in the country.
Formed during the Haripura Session of the Indian National Congress under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru, initiated by Subhas Chandra Bose.

key_associations.extra_info: Officially titled 'A Brief Memorandum Outlining a Plan of Economic Development for India', it advocated for state intervention in the economic development of the nation.
A plan heavily focused on the decentralized development of agriculture and cottage industries.
Based on a Marxist approach, this plan prioritized both agricultural and industrial development to meet the basic needs of the people.
Inspired by the Sarvodaya ideals of Acharya Vinoba Bhave, emphasizing self-reliance and decentralized planning.

sections.title: Planning Commission: Establishment and Structure
sections.description: The Planning Commission was the central agency of the Government of India responsible for assessing the country's resources and drafting the Five-Year Plans.

key_concepts.explanation: The Planning Commission was neither mentioned in the Constitution of India nor created by an Act of Parliament. It was created purely by an executive order.
A centralized policy-making model where economic plans were formulated at the central level by the Commission and then implemented across the states.

historical_events.significance: Formed via an Executive Resolution of the Union Cabinet, based on the recommendations of the K.C. Neogy Advisory Planning Board (1946).

important_facts.fact: The Prime Minister of India served as the Ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission.
Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Chairman, and Gulzarilal Nanda was appointed as the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

sections.title: National Development Council (NDC)
sections.description: The NDC was established as the highest decision-making authority in the country for matters related to development planning and final approval of the Five-Year Plans.

key_concepts.explanation: Because states had no direct representation in the Planning Commission, the NDC was created to include State Chief Ministers, ensuring their participation in the national planning process.

historical_events.significance: Like the Planning Commission, the NDC was also created by an executive resolution as a non-constitutional and non-statutory body.

important_facts.fact: Prominent political scientist K. Santhanam described the National Development Council as a 'Super Cabinet' due to its overarching influence on national policy.

sections.title: Major Types of Economic Planning
sections.description: Economic planning can be classified into different models based on the level of state control and the nature of the economic system.

key_concepts.explanation: Adopted in socialist and communist economies (like the former USSR), where the state owns all resources, and the central planning authority sets mandatory targets for all sectors.

Practiced in mixed economies, where the state provides broad guidelines and targets, but relies on market mechanisms and incentivizes the private sector to achieve them. India officially shifted to this from the 8th Five-Year Plan.

A concept advocated by Gunnar Myrdal, where the performance of the plan is assessed every year, and a new plan is made for the next year. It was implemented in India during 1978-1980 by the Janata Party government.

sections.title: End of Planning Commission and Rise of NITI Aayog
sections.description: Realizing that the decades-old centralized planning model was ill-equipped for a modern, liberalized economy, the government replaced it with a new think tank.

historical_events.significance: The Government of India officially scrapped the 64-year-old Planning Commission to make way for a more dynamic and decentralized institution.
The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) was established to replace the Planning Commission as the premier policy think tank.

important_facts.fact: Unlike the Planning Commission's 'Top-Down' approach, NITI Aayog operates on a 'Bottom-Up' approach, strongly emphasizing Cooperative Federalism.
Montek Singh Ahluwalia holds the historical distinction of being the last Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.
